name: Discover Skill Capabilities
query: What can you help me do with Conductor?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Activate the conductor skill from natural-language intent (no slash command typed)

Step 2: Summarize the major capability groups from SKILL.md: workflow CRUD, execution, monitoring, management, signaling, scheduling, worker scaffolding, visualization, review/optimization, AI/LLM workflows (LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE, MCP, RAG), and building Conductor Agents — SDK-native (`Agent` + `@tool`, run/deploy/serve) or bring-your-framework (LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents, Google ADK, Vercel AI, Claude Agent SDK), invoked from workflows via the `AGENT` task (see references/agents.md)

Step 3: Mention that schedules are part of OSS (not Orkes-only). If secrets come up: `${workflow.secrets.X}` works on OSS too — the server resolves it from `CONDUCTOR_SECRET_X` env vars (and the agent runtime exposes the store at `/api/secrets`); Orkes adds a managed secret store and the `conductor secret` CLI. Webhooks are Orkes-only.
Step 4: Offer concrete sample requests the user can make (e.g. 'create a workflow that...', 'review my workflow', 'schedule X daily')

Step 5: Optionally mention the slash-command shortcuts that exist on Claude Code (/conductor-setup, /conductor-optimize, /conductor-scaffold-worker, /conductor-scaffold-agent) but emphasize plain English works too
Step 6: Ask what the user wants to do next
success_criteria: Agent does not require a slash command to discover capabilities — natural language triggers the skill

At least 8 of the 11 major capability areas (create, run, monitor, manage, signal, schedule, optimize, visualize, workers, AI/LLM workflows, building/deploying agents) are mentioned at least once. Smaller/terser models may consolidate categories (e.g. group manage + signal under 'control') — that's fine as long as the underlying functions are covered.

Agent-building is listed as a capability: Conductor Agents via the SDK (or bringing a LangChain / LangGraph / OpenAI Agents / Google ADK / Vercel AI / Claude Agent SDK agent), deployed and invoked from workflows via the `AGENT` task
Schedules are correctly described as OSS, not Orkes-only

If secrets are mentioned, `${workflow.secrets.X}` itself is not described as Orkes-only (it works on OSS via `CONDUCTOR_SECRET_*` server env vars); calling the managed store / `conductor secret` CLI and webhooks Orkes-only is correct
Sample queries are concrete and actionable, not vague
Agent ends by asking what the user wants to do (not by dumping the entire skill content)
